name: Lockdown screws
function: Radial screws in the tubing head (and in some casing spools) that engage the hanger neck to hold it down against pressure from below and to energize the hanger seal on some designs.

tabs.overview: Each screw runs through a packing gland in the head wall so it can be run in under pressure. They are run in to a specified torque and the count is checked; all screws in and torqued is a hold point before pressure is applied.
tabs.engineering: Screw size, number, and torque per the OEM; gland packing rated to the head pressure.
tabs.safety: Screws are run in only against a landed hanger; running screws against an empty bowl damages the bowl. Gland packing leaks are a common source of small wellhead leaks.
tabs.evidence: API 6A (S1) for pressure-containing parts and connections; public OEM pages (S2, S3, S5, S11, S12) for configurations; field and manufacturing practice (S9).

hazards.control: Pressure test before pumping; bleed down and verify zero before breaking any connection.
